docs: add plan review for plan-review governance (209)

result_json.summary: Well-layered translation of 206 into a pure policy core, append-only decision fold, and thin adapters, but not ready: Phase 8 targets a dashboard slice with no plan (human scope decision), the gate CAS lets two racing submitters both win, human-resolved gate causes re-gate every round, and prior-finding outcomes have no representation compatible with emit readiness and plan-208 R arithmetic. Advisory-mode strictness also needs a policy decision; remaining items are mechanical.

baselineAssessment.reason: Independent per-surface estimate of the initial scope: protocol+plan-diff validation 5, pure domain/closure/fingerprint 5, decisions/fold/index/migration 8, routing 3, gate prompt+decision command+CAS 8, recording integration+context injection 5, templates/skills 3, dashboard 8 (priced for uncertainty: slice 04 has no plan), run-state/docs 3 since tests belong to the items they validate

items.title: Phase 8 (W8) is planned against slice 04, which has no plan, code, or contracts; split into a follow-on plan or hold the whole plan
items.reason: 04-control-plane-dashboard.plan-input.md is draft with no generated plan and src/dashboard does not exist, so Phase 8 has no concrete paths or verifiable gate and 8 points of pure uncertainty are frozen into B0. Scope decision: move Phase 8/W8 and dashboard parity tests to a post-slice-04 plan (recommended; unblocks the rest once 208 merges) or hold the entire plan until slice 04 is merged and re-plan Phase 8.

items.title: Gate CAS is keyed by per-submission decisionId, so racing terminal/dashboard submitters both append a decision
items.reason: decision:review:<decisionId> with a fresh UUID per submission plus check-then-act across PromptStore (SQLite) and RecordStore (JSONL) in separate processes lets two contradictory decisions resolve one gate. Lowest-cost fix: gate-scoped key decision:review-gate:<gateId> written with the human step in one RecordStore.atomicAppendIfAllNew batch (plan-208 primitive) as the single CAS; records first, prompt answer as best-effort projection; drop the answered-prompt repair direction and expected-decision-sequence field; add a cross-process race contract test.

items.title: Human-resolved gate causes are re-derived every round and re-open the gate indefinitely
items.reason: Plan-208 deriveBudget recomputes baseline_disputed from immutable I vs B0 and positive_architecture_exceeded from cumulative P on every snapshot; routing step 2 gates on them and step 1 only removes accepted-risk findings, so after retain/adjust baseline or approve_architecture_burden each later closure review opens a new gate. Add a precedence step and matrix rows that drop gate causes covered by an active unsuperseded decision (baseline dispute once per run; architecture until P or single-item set grows past the approval), keep alerts visible in the budget decoration, and record resolvedBy decisionId.

items.title: Prior-finding outcomes have no wire representation compatible with emit readiness and plan-208 R arithmetic
items.reason: priorFindingStatus on VerdictItem forces addressed findings into items[]: protocol emit turns --ready plus any item into ready_with_corrections, plan-208 computePendingR sums every listed item into R, and advisory/v1 routing hands them to the author, so an all-addressed closure review can never be ready. Add top-level priorFindings[{id,status}] with a repeatable --prior-finding flag, keep items[] to still-blocking work (partially_addressed/still_open carried under the same ID with remaining effortDelta), define the required-outcome set (not yet addressed and not covered by an active defer/accept decision), and persist it in the snapshot extension with tests.

items.title: Decide whether fail-closed closure convergence applies in advisory (default) mode and what a mid-run mode change does
items.reason: Section 3.3 runs fail-closed validateClosureReview on all active budget runs and Phase 7 rewrites the single continued template, so default advisory users get convergence enforced (verdicts rejected, ordinary missed issues barred from items[]) although 206 section 7 says advisory does not change routing and section 8.2 stages convergence under Enforced. Policy choice: downgrade closure-evidence violations to recorded diagnostics in advisory with mode-conditional template prose (recommended), or apply as written and document it as a default-behavior change; also state behavior when mode changes between rounds since mode is live config.

items.title: Human decisions (scope trade, deferral, re-estimate) are never delivered to the plan author
items.reason: author-process-plan-review.md receives only review_path, plan_path, user_notes, and run_id and tells the author to address the review items, so a deferred finding is still implemented and removed scope is unknown; the durable decision has no effect on W. Reuse the section 6.3 projection to append a governing-decisions block (finding IDs to skip, retained/removed scope, re-estimate request, governing B) to author-process-plan-review renders in native and invoke paths; add the template to Phase 7 and Files Touched with a render test.

items.title: Rendered plan diff is truncated at 200 lines, so exact-diff-shown validation cannot accept valid citations on large revisions
items.reason: getFileDiffSummary (src/git.ts:205-224) caps the appended diff at 200 lines and section 3.2 validates against the rendered context with oversized-diff rejection, so a regression introduced beyond line 200 can never be legally cited and the verdict fails closed with nothing recorded. Build the full plan-only patch and hunk hashes in buildPlanReviewDiffContext and validate against that; make truncation render-only with the commit range and remaining hunk headers listed; keep binary rejection; have INTRODUCED_HUNK_NOT_FOUND name the closest hunk header.

items.title: Gate identity/authority is ambiguous: random UUID plus mutable state in the coordination store is not rebuildable from records
items.reason: Section 2.2 stores open gate state in SQLite with a random gateId while section 2.3 claims review_gate_index is rebuildable and section 6.1 creates the gate after the reviewer record; wiping .5x or crashing in between loses the gate and the ID decisions must reference. Lowest-cost fix: derive the gate purely (latest plan-reviewer step has route human_gate and no decision carries its gate key) with a deterministic gateId from runId, snapshot id, and sorted causes; superseded means a newer snapshot exists; prompt and index are projections; remove gate record-line codecs.

items.title: Decisions stream already carries human-step and answered-prompt kinds; one gate resolution yields three lines and fail-closed decoding would flag existing runs
items.reason: recordStepInternal mirrors every human:* step into decisions (run-v1.handler.ts:2151-2164) and answered prompts append answered-prompt lines (prompt.handler.ts:225-257). State that fold, index, run-state, and timeline select only kind plan-review-governance, ignore existing kinds silently, and treat only unknown governance versions as diagnostics; write human:review-governance through the shared seam without the generic human-step mirror; add a three-kind fixture to fold/reindex tests.

items.title: Reconcile with the code-complete plan-208 branch now and add the missing explicit Phase 0
items.reason: The Overview defers to a Phase 0 that does not exist. On 5x/208-review-budget-advisory-plan: PlanReviewBudgetContext does not exist (ReviewBudgetCommandContext; paired writer is recordPlanReviewerStepWithSnapshot, which applyPlanReviewGovernance must compose with rather than parallel); VerdictItem already has the budget fields and creditClaim; mode enforced is reserved with ENFORCED_REVIEW_BUDGET_WARNING, a run-state not-implemented string, and a config description that no phase removes; applyPlanReviewBudget reads baseline.b so an additive governingBaseline input is needed; post-decision forecasts must be a pure deriveBudget recompute, not a new snapshot line (snapshot to reviewer step is 1:1). Add a Phase 0 reconciliation checklist and correct these names and tasks.

items.title: Follow-up count and adjacent-debt gate requests have missing or contradictory representations
items.reason: followUpCount and repeatable follow-up records have no source field while section 3.1 forbids new flags and 206 section 6.2 keeps follow-ups in the review document only; section 1.3 rejects adjacent debt as a blocking item while routing step 2 gates on an unresolved adjacent-debt scope request. Keep follow-ups in Markdown and drop followUpCount and the emit bullet; state once per 206 section 4.2 that adjacent coupling is allowed only as a human_required item (gate, no credit) and unrelated is rejected from items[].

items.title: All-zero architecture deltas understate gross positive burden P
items.reason: The plan adds a new subsystem, a new authoritative record kind with fold and index migration (W2), and a new cross-process gate/decision boundary plus CLI command group (W5), and its own Surface Snapshot lists 3 new shared abstractions and 1 schema; 206 section 4.1 scores new maintenance burden positively. Rescore at least W2 and W5 (+2 each) and W1 (+1) with rationale; this stays under the positive-architecture limit for B0 52.

result_json.guidance: P0.1: Defer dashboard work: remove Phase 8/W8 and dashboard parity tests from this slice; preserve them as an explicit follow-up after slice 04 merges. P1.1: Pin review-budget mode per run at baseline activation. Advisory mode records closure/convergence diagnostics but does not reject verdicts or change routing; enforced mode validates and routes. Later config changes affect only new runs. Apply all auto-fix findings P0.2-P0.4, P1.2-P1.7, and P2.1 exactly as recommended by the review.

result_json.message: docs: revise plan 209 after governance review
docs: update plan review for plan-review governance (209) v1.1

result_json.summary: v1.1 resolves all four original P0s and every P1/P2 except two residuals: the gate-key loser path breaks the plan-208 finalize seam (P0.2) and gateId is hashed from causes that change on resolution (P1.4). New mechanical gaps: typed prompt payload path (P1.8), post-decision routing (P1.9), numbering (P2.2), and stale-gate side effects (P2.3). All remaining items are auto_fix; none needs a human decision.

items.title: Gate-key loser path breaks the plan-208 finalize seam: duplicate or losing submissions spin or throw instead of observing the winner
items.reason: Design is now correct (gate-scoped decision:review-gate:<gateId> plus human step in one atomicAppendIfAllNew), but a loser arriving after the winner builds step key N+1 (new) plus the existing gate key, so the batch returns created:false with no step line. finalizeAndWritePreparedStep then retries up to maxSteps for omitted iteration and throws RECORD_ITERATION_RETRY_EXHAUSTED, or throws RECORD_PAIR_CORRUPT for an explicit iteration. Fix: route the write through finalizeAndWritePreparedStep with mode paired-all-new and extraOps for the decision op, pre-read the gate key, extend the seam so !created checks extra-op keys first and returns a coupled-key-exists outcome instead of retrying or throwing, and add simultaneous-loser and after-winner-loser contract tests.

items.title: gateId is hashed from causes that change when the gate is resolved; multi-cause gates are unspecified
items.reason: gateId hashes sorted causes, but causes are the post-suppression result of the decision fold, so after retain_baseline or approve_architecture_burden the recomputed gateId differs from decision:review-gate:<gateId> and the resolved gate looks unresolved or a different gate appears; a baseline dispute plus over_effective gate resolved by one decision covering one cause is also undefined. Fix: hash gateId from the causes persisted in the reviewer snapshot at record time, define resolved as the gate key existing, and after each decision recompute remaining uncovered causes and derive one deterministic successor gate from (runId, snapshotId, remaining causes, predecessor gateId); add a two-cause test where the first decision leaves exactly one successor and the resolved gate never reopens.

items.title: Typed gate prompt cannot carry a decision payload and the generic prompt-answer path is unspecified
items.reason: PromptStore.answerPrompt takes a single answer string while decisions need rationale, evidence, scope and baseline fields; the plan does not say what happens when a plan_review_gate prompt is answered through the generic prompt path instead of 5x review decide, which would leave an answered prompt and answered-prompt line with no decision. Fix: make the gate prompt a notification and wait handle only, have the generic answer path reject plan_review_gate prompts with a structured error pointing at 5x review decide, have the prompt-wait function poll the gate-key decision rather than the prompt answer, and add rejection and wait tests to section 5.3.

items.title: Post-decision routing and skill resume are unspecified; a not_ready verdict whose blockers were all deferred has no route
items.reason: submitPlanReviewDecision returns a route and section 7.4 says resume from the durable decision, but no rule derives it; routing step 5 requires ready and step 7 requires remaining required corrections, so a not_ready verdict whose only blocking items were deferred matches neither. Fix: define routeAfterDecision as a re-run of derivePlanReviewGovernance on the latest recorded verdict with the new fold and add matrix rows: deferral leaving zero required items routes to complete; increase_budget or retain_baseline routes to author_revision or final_corrections if qualifying; trade_scope or request_author_reestimate routes to author_revision; abort is terminal; have review gate show and review decide return that route for the skill branch.

items.title: Phase and work-item numbering skips 8 after the dashboard removal
items.reason: The table of contents, phase headings, timeline and W-rows jump from Phase 7/W7 to Phase 9/W9; renumber or add a one-line note that Phase 8/W8 is intentionally vacant so readers do not assume a missing phase.

items.title: Side effects on a stale gate: abort or baseline change can run after a decision that no longer governs
items.reason: Section 5.2 validates the expected forecast before the append and applies side effects after it; a newer reviewer snapshot landing between the two leaves a decision retained for audit but not governing while an abort or baseline-change side effect still runs. Fix: re-check that the gate is still the current derived gate after the append and, if stale, skip side effects, keep the line as audit only and return REVIEW_GATE_STALE.

result_json.message: docs: update plan review for plan-review governance (209) v1.2

result_json.summary: v1.2 closes P0.2, P1.8, P2.2 and P2.3: the finalize-seam loser path, prompt-as-notification, vacant-ID note and post-append stale check are all sound. Two closure residuals remain in the new gate-lifecycle rules: cause-coverage is undefined for most choices and persisted causes are described as unsuppressed (P1.4), and routeAfterDecision precedence conflicts with itself and does not filter deferred findings (P1.9). Two polish items: review decide input contract (P2.4) and W5 effort saturation (P2.5). All remaining items are auto_fix.

items.title: Gate cause coverage is undefined for most choices, and persisting unsuppressed causes contradicts P0.3
items.reason: Section 2.2 persists the reviewers pre-decision unsuppressed gate causes, which read literally ignores earlier decisions and would re-include a baseline dispute already retained in an earlier round; persist record-time effective causes (after folding prior decisions) and keep suppressed ones as resolvedBy audit entries. The successor chain also depends on uncovered causes, but coverage is defined only for baseline dispute and architecture approval; add one choice-by-cause table: increase_budget and adjust_baseline change B so the band is recomputed, defer_accept_risk covers causes tied to the deferred finding IDs, trade_scope/request_author_reestimate/abort close the gate with no successor, and approve_architecture_burden covers the architecture cause within its envelope.

items.title: routeAfterDecision precedence rules conflict and deferred findings are not filtered before budget recompute
items.reason: Section 4.3 returns a successor human_gate for uncovered causes before choice-specific routing yet says trade_scope and request_author_reestimate always return author_revision; increase_budget/adjust_baseline/retain_baseline return final_corrections or author_revision even when the recorded verdict was ready with only a baseline dispute, where the rerun of derivePlanReviewGovernance yields complete; and budget recompute does not say findings covered by an active deferral are removed before deriveBudget, so deferring the over-budget finding re-gates forever. Fix: make the rerun of derivePlanReviewGovernance on the recomputed budget authoritative, limit choice-specific overrides to trade_scope, request_author_reestimate and abort (which skip the successor check), filter deferred findings before deriveBudget and readiness routing, derive the abort route before running the terminal handler as a side effect, and update the section 4.4 rows.

items.title: The 5x review decide input contract is unspecified
items.reason: The decision payload needs rationale, an evidence array, retained/removed scope, finding refs and a baseline change, but the plan does not say how a terminal caller supplies them and section 9.3 documents only review gate/decision commands. Specify one form: --gate, --choice, --rationale, repeatable --evidence/--finding/--retain/--remove, --baseline, plus --input-json or stdin for the full payload, and print requiredFieldsByChoice from review gate show, so skills and CLI docs agree.

items.title: W5 is saturated at the top of the effort scale after v1.2 scope additions
items.reason: W5 is scored 8, the maximum on the plan-208 rubric, yet v1.2 added a shared finalize-seam extension with its own test file, PromptStore rejection in two implementations plus migration, a decision-key wait helper, and stale-check plumbing, so the added work is unscored. Split the notification/wait/prompt-store work into a new row (for example W10, since W8 is not reused) at about 3 points and keep CAS, seam and decision handler in W5; the total rises to about 47, still under B0 52.

result_json.message: docs: update plan review for plan-review governance (209) v1.3

result_json.summary: v1.3 closes P1.4, P1.9, P2.4 and P2.5: effective-cause persistence with a full choice-to-cause table, authoritative filtered-budget rerun with limited overrides, a single review decide input contract, and W10 split (ledger 47, under B0 52). One residual: baseline-dispute coverage is scoped to a single snapshot, so retain/adjust/re-estimate re-gate the immutable I-vs-B0 dispute every round (P0.3). One polish item: review decide --finding should not require a caller-authored fingerprint (P2.6). Both are auto_fix.

items.title: Baseline dispute coverage is scoped to one snapshot, so retain/adjust/re-estimate re-gate the same dispute every later round
items.reason: v1.3 says retain_baseline covers this snapshots dispute, adjust_baseline resolves the snapshots dispute by folding B, and request_author_reestimate does not suppress; but plan-208 deriveBudget computes baseline_disputed from abs(I minus B0) on every snapshot and both are immutable, so a folded B never clears it and the next round first gate re-opens the same dispute, the original P0.3 failure and a contradiction of the plans own section 4.4 row that retained/adjusted baseline does not re-gate. Fix: treat the dispute as run-level so an active unsuperseded retain_baseline or adjust_baseline covers it for every later snapshot with resolvedBy (adjust also folds B into the bands); state request_author_reestimate behavior explicitly (recommended: intentionally does not cover it, and the next gate offers only retain/adjust/abort so re-estimate cannot loop); update the section 2 Resolved causes paragraph, the section 2.2 table and section 4.1 step 2 consistently; add a routing row that a round-1 retained or adjusted baseline does not re-enter round-2 first-gate causes.

items.title: review decide --finding asks the operator to author a CLI-derived fingerprint
items.reason: The terminal contract requires --finding with a FindingIdentity JSON object including a sha256 fingerprint that neither a human nor the orchestrating agent can produce reliably. Accept --finding <id> and have the CLI resolve and validate the fingerprint against the latest snapshot, keep the JSON form only inside --input-json, and print each finding ID and fingerprint in review gate show.

result_json.message: docs: update plan review for plan-review governance (209) v1.4

result_json.summary: v1.4 closes P0.3 (run-level retain/adjust baseline resolution with a non-looping re-estimate policy, consistent across the design paragraph, coverage table, routing step 2 and tests) and P2.6 (ID-only --finding with CLI fingerprint resolution). One new determinism gap: acceptance-time staleness has no cross-stream ordering source and the post-append stale check is racy (P1.10); the fix uses steps-stream order of the atomically appended human step. It is auto_fix.

items.title: Acceptance-time staleness has no deterministic ordering source and the post-append stale check is racy
items.reason: Sections 2.1 and 5.2 make a decisions effect depend on whether its forecastId was current when accepted, but reviewer snapshots live in the budget stream, decisions in the decisions stream, and steps in the steps stream, with insertion order defined only within a stream and created_at second-resolution, so a fold or reindex over a wiped index cannot distinguish accepted-then-newer-snapshot from appended-after-newer-snapshot; and section 5.2 re-reads the latest snapshot after the append, so a reviewer step landing between append and re-read returns REVIEW_GATE_STALE and skips side effects (including abort) while the record-derived fold applies the decision. Fix: the decision is appended atomically with its human:review-governance step and reviewer steps share the steps stream, so define stale-at-acceptance as a plan-reviewer step existing between the gates reviewer step and the decision human step in steps insertion order; use that rule in the fold, in reindexReviewGovernance, and in the section 5.2 post-append check instead of re-reading the latest snapshot; add contract tests for reviewer-step-before and reviewer-step-after the human step and a rebuild-equals-live test.

result_json.guidance: Authorize one final correction cycle beyond maxReviewIterations. Resolve P1.10 exactly as recommended: define stale-at-acceptance from steps-stream insertion order, where a plan-reviewer step between the gate reviewer step and the atomically appended human:review-governance step makes the decision stale; use the same rule in the live handler, governance fold, and reindex; replace the post-append latest-snapshot read; add reviewer-before, reviewer-after, and rebuild-equals-live tests.

result_json.message: docs: update plan review for plan-review governance (209) v1.5

result_json.summary: v1.5 closes the last open item, P1.10: staleness is now defined solely from steps-stream insertion order via one classifyDecisionAcceptance helper shared by live handling, the fold, and reindexReviewGovernance, resolved through plan-208's existing snapshot-to-step key and a decisionId/gateId stamped on the paired human step, with fail-closed handling for malformed boundaries and reviewer-before/after plus rebuild-equals-live tests. I traced the original race against the new rule and it resolves correctly, and found no stray contradictory wording or new issue in this or prior addenda. All P0/P1/P2 findings across every round are now closed; the plan is ready for implementation.
